Upstream base: lsalzman/enet at 5a9c537fd464b3c6d3c55e1d3bd47588faf71b42.

Local source changes:
- peer.c: zero-initialize newly allocated incoming fragment-reassembly storage
  when data is NULL. Both reliable and unreliable fragment reception use this
  path. This prevents unwritten gaps from exposing uninitialized memory without
  changing enet_packet_create(NULL, ...) or adding fragment-coverage validation.
  Matches radkesvat/enet commit 2a2312fa92c437abfb626140434230f19a6b490a.
- peer.c: include packet/command structures and fragment bitmaps, in addition to
  payload bytes, in totalWaitingData. Release the identical charge on delivery
  and discard, validate fragment count before allocation, and reject size-sum
  overflow. Preserve the existing admission threshold and its one-packet
  overshoot. Allocator overhead and application-owned packets are not charged.
- include/enet/enet.h: document the updated receive counter and threshold units;
  public structure layouts and the wire protocol are unchanged.

WaterWall-specific integration lives outside it:
- tunnels/Internals/EnetCommon/src/platform.c replaces unix.c and win32.c in
  production builds.
- tests/enet_vendor_source_policy_test.py pins every vendored file to the
  upstream base plus the local source changes above.
